transcript: The romcom is back. I'm fully late on this one, just watched voicemails for Isabelle, and, goodness, did this scratch an itch that I didn't know I needed. This brought me right back to being 12 years old, watching 10 things I hate about you for the very first time. I grew up in what I think is the heyday of the romantic comedy, the 90s and early 2000s and it has been so long since I've seen a romantic comedy that feels like that time. To be clear, it takes place now. It is a present day film, but it just gave me those feelings of nostalgia. And I don't know if it's because of the, like, kind of unhinged premise of the film or the fact that, like, the two of them are ridiculously charming and have so much chemistry, or if it's the montages, cause this soundtrack. Mmm. 10 out of 10. 10 out of 10. It was How to lose a guy in 10 days. It was Bridget Jones's Diary sleepless in Seattle. It was giving me all of that. Despite everything that I just said. It also feels very original, which I loved I love the fact that it felt like it came from that era, but still stood entirely on its own. And it's because this movie is about two different love stories. you Have the love story of Jill and Wes falling in love. But I think more importantly, you Have the love story of Jill and her sister Isabelle And it's a grief story. And I love the fact that this film doesn't expect Jill to move on from her grief to fall in love. Jill never stops grieving. Will never stop grieving her sister. But she also can meet someone and fall in love even though her sister isn't there. I just wanna cry talking about it. Anyway, should we examine the logistics and the like? Slight stalking too closely? No. It's a ROM com. ROM com rules apply. But, uh, I just really loved it.
